indicators.name: dengue_mortality_rate
indicators.title: Dengue mortality
indicators.description: Number of deaths due to dengue, identified by ICD-10 codes A90 and A91, per 100.000 inhabitants in the population residing in a given geographic territory during the analyzed annual period. This indicator estimates the risk of death from dengue in a specific population over a defined time interval, reflecting the severity of the disease and its magnitude as a public health problem, as well as highlighting possible differences in population vulnerability, access to healthcare, and the quality of clinical management. It also allows for the analysis of population, spatial, and temporal variations in dengue mortality, identifying higher-risk groups and areas, and supports the planning, management, and evaluation of surveillance, healthcare, and disease control actions.It is calculated as the number of dengue deaths in a given period divided by the resident population in the same period, multiplied by 100.000.

indicators.name: dengue_incidence_rate
indicators.title: Dengue incidence
indicators.description: Number of new confirmed dengue cases, identified by ICD-10 code A90, per 100.000 inhabitants in the resident population of a given geographic territory during the analyzed annual period. This indicator estimates the risk of dengue occurrence in a specific population over a defined time interval, considering exposure to illness in endemic or epidemic contexts. It supports the analysis of population, spatial, and temporal variations in confirmed cases and informs the planning, management, and evaluation of epidemiological surveillance and vector control actions. It is calculated as the number of new confirmed dengue cases in a given period divided by the resident population in the same period, multiplied by 100.000.

indicators.name: zika_incidence_rate
indicators.title: Zika incidence
indicators.description: Number of new confirmed Zika cases, identified by ICD-10 code A92.5, per 100.000 inhabitants in the resident population of a given geographic territory during the analyzed annual period. This indicator estimates the risk of Zika occurrence in a specific population over a defined time interval, considering exposure to illness. It supports the analysis of population, spatial, and temporal variations in confirmed cases, informing the planning, management, and evaluation of epidemiological surveillance, prevention, and vector control actions, as well as the monitoring of vulnerable populations, especially pregnant women. It is calculated as the number of new confirmed Zika cases in a given period divided by the resident population in the same period, multiplied by 100.000.

indicators.name: chickungunya_incidence_rate
indicators.title: Chikungunya incidence
indicators.description: Number of new confirmed chikungunya cases, identified by ICD-10 code A92.0, per 100.000 inhabitants in the resident population of a given geographic territory during the analyzed annual period. This indicator estimates the risk of chikungunya occurrence in a specific population over a defined time interval, particularly in epidemic contexts, considering exposure to illness. It supports the analysis of population, spatial, and temporal variations in confirmed cases, informing the planning, management, and evaluation of epidemiological surveillance and vector control policies and actions. It is calculated as the number of new confirmed chikungunya cases in a given period divided by the resident population in the same period, multiplied by 100.000.

indicators.name: yellow_fever_incidence_rate
indicators.title: Yellow fever incidence
indicators.description: Number of new confirmed yellow fever cases, including both sylvatic and urban forms, identified by ICD-10 code A95, per 100.000 inhabitants in the resident population of a given geographic territory during the analyzed annual period. This indicator estimates the risk of yellow fever occurrence in a specific population over a defined time interval, considering exposure to infection. It supports the analysis of population, spatial, and temporal variations in confirmed cases, informing the planning, management, and evaluation of epidemiological surveillance, vaccination strategies, and vector control actions in risk areas. It is calculated as the number of new confirmed yellow fever cases in a given period divided by the resident population in the same period, multiplied by 100.000.

indicators.name: chagas_disease_incidence_rate
indicators.title: Chagas disease incidence
indicators.description: Number of new confirmed cases of acute Chagas disease, identified by ICD-10 code B57.0, per 100.000 inhabitants in the resident population of a given geographic territory during the analyzed annual period. This indicator estimates the risk of occurrence of new Chagas disease cases in a specific population over a defined time interval, considering exposure to infection. It supports the analysis of population, spatial, and temporal variations in confirmed cases, informing the planning, management, and evaluation of epidemiological surveillance actions, vector control, food safety measures, and outbreak monitoring, especially in areas with active transmission. It is calculated as the number of new confirmed Chagas disease cases in a given period divided by the resident population in the same period, multiplied by 100.000.

indicators.name: dengue_cases_notified
indicators.title: Dengue cases
indicators.description: Shows the number of dengue cases notified each week. The values are retrospectively updated every week to reflect the most accurate data available.

indicators.name: dengue_incidence_rate
indicators.title: Dengue incidence
indicators.description: Is a representation of the estimated incidence rate of dengue, calculated as the number of reported cases per population, multiplied by 100.00. It provides a standardized measure to compare dengue occurrence relative to the size of the population.

indicators.name: dengue_alert_level
indicators.title: Dengue alert level
indicators.description: Is a classification that indicates the current risk of dengue outbreaks in a given region. This level ranges from 1 to 4, as follows: 1 (Green): Low risk - situation under control. 2 (Yellow): Moderate risk - caution advised. 3 (Orange): High risk - alert for potential outbreak. 4 (Red): Very high risk - critical situation with epidemic potential.

indicators.name: dengue_confirmed_cases
indicators.title: Dengue confirmed cases
indicators.description: Is a number of dengue cases that have been definitively confirmed through laboratory testing. It reflects only those cases for which diagnostic tests have validated the presence of the dengue virus, ensuring accuracy in reporting and surveillance.
